definitions.gloss: depreciation; writing off an asset over time
definitions.explanation: Spreading the cost of a long-lived asset such as a building, machine, or vehicle across the years it is used, instead of treating the whole purchase as an expense at once.

examples.japanese: {減価償却|げんかしょうきゃく}の{計算|けいさん}をする。
この{機械|きかい}は{五年|ごねん}かけて{減価償却|げんかしょうきゃく}する。
examples.english: This machine is depreciated over five years.

examples.japanese: {建物|たてもの}の{減価償却費|げんかしょうきゃくひ}が{毎年|まいとし}{経費|けいひ}として{計上|けいじょう}される。
examples.english: Depreciation expense on the building is recorded as a cost every year.

examples.japanese: {減価償却|げんかしょうきゃく}が{終|お}わった{設備|せつび}でも、まだ{十分|じゅうぶん}に{使|つか}えることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Equipment that has been fully depreciated can often still be used perfectly well.

notes:
Formed from {減価|げんか} (decline in value) + {償却|しょうきゃく} (writing off). Takes する to form a verb, and combines with {費|ひ} in {減価償却費|げんかしょうきゃくひ} (depreciation expense), which is what actually appears on the income statement.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {減価償却|げんかしょうきゃく}する: to depreciate an asset
- {減価償却費|げんかしょうきゃくひ}: depreciation expense
- {減価償却|げんかしょうきゃく}が{終|お}わる: to be fully depreciated

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {償却|しょうきゃく}: writing off — the broader term, also used for debts
- {耐用年数|たいようねんすう}: useful life — the number of years used for the calculation
- {原価|げんか}: cost price — the cost of producing goods, unrelated despite the similar sound
